chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from al-ʿAmrakī al-Būfakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man: is it proper for him to pour water from his mouth and wash with it the thing that may be in his garment? He said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: a man; the person about whom the ruling is being asked
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water; the purifying substance being used
key_terms.ثَوْبِهِ: his garment; the clothing being cleaned
key_terms.سَأَلْتُهُ: I asked him; introducing the legal question posed to the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.فِيهِ: his mouth; the source from which the water is poured
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَصُبَّ: to pour; to let water flow out for use
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he washes; the act of cleansing

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use water poured from the mouth to wash impurity from clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning taharah and the removal of najasah from clothing. Imam Mūsā عليه السلام states that there is no problem in using water poured from the mouth to wash something on one’s garment.
